Maria: quick probe — we need to pick AZ strategies for inference fleets next q. two options i'm modeling:
Maria: 1) Single-AZ reserved capacity (cheaper reserved GPU hours) + cross-AZ LB failover (egress + inter-AZ traffic).
Maria: 2) Multi-AZ reserved split (smaller reserved pools per AZ) to avoid inter-AZ egress but more fragmented commitments.
Maria: TL;DR: tradeoff is reserved-utilization vs egress + slightly higher p99.
Jon: can you drop the assumptions (gpu type, unit costs, egress) you used?
Maria: pasted quick numbers (very rough):
Maria: ```
GPU: H100-like
On-demand: $18.0/hr
1yr reserved (committed): $11.5/hr
3yr reserved: $8.8/hr
Inter-AZ egress: $0.02/GB
Cross-region egress: $0.12/GB
Avg tokens/sec per GPU: 325
Target p99 latency headroom: 50ms
```
Priya: thanks. curious what inter-AZ traffic volume you assumed for single-AZ + LB? inter-AZ adds both cost + ~1.2-2.5ms tail latency typically.
Maria: i simulated 3 workload mixes:
Maria: - steady: 70% util, low burst; inter-AZ 40GB/hr
Maria: - spiky: 50% util, big peaks; inter-AZ 140GB/hr
Maria: - bursty-mixed: 60% util, 80GB/hr
Maria: Results (per-region normalized $/effective-gpu-hr):
Maria: ```
Single-AZ reserved + inter-AZ: normalized cost = 1.00 (baseline)
Multi-AZ split reserved: normalized cost = 1.08 (+8%) but inter-AZ traffic ~0
Single-AZ on-demand: normalized cost = 1.27 (+27%)
Notes: spiky workload, single-AZ + burst capacity (on-demand) pushed egress costs up ~3-5% of bill.
```
Max: that +8% for multi-AZ is believable. split reservations reduce bin-packing efficiency. did you model ability to move capacity between AZs (fast failover) or pre-warm?
Maria: modeled fast failover (automated LB weight shifts) but not full live migration of large KV caches — so some wasted cold-start tokens. that hurts p99 on certain requests.
Ella: what about networking SKU differences? in eu-west cloud provider we get lower inter-AZ-than-us egress but also different reserved discounts per AZ (some AZs have a lower 1yr price). did you run per-AZ pricing variants?
Maria: yes — per-AZ delta is small for GPU hourly (up to 4%) but egress and cross-AZ private interconnect pricing varies: some AZ pairs have negotiated private rates (we can route on those if constrained).
Jon: ops question: if we go single-AZ reserved, what's our SLO risk in terms of p99 against AZ outages? do we rely on fallback model variant in other AZs?
Priya: fallback plan is: synchronous fallback to smaller quantized model in another AZ + async requeue to original model. that keeps tail availability but increases p99 for full-quality responses.
Priya: we measured in canary: fallback path p95 ~ 180ms, p99 ~ 420ms (compared to baseline p95 55ms, p99 85ms).
deploy-bot: canary/az-fallback-test finished — 3 failures (timed out) out of 12k requests, rate 0.025% :white_check_mark:
Max: can we monetize the increased latency? customers on enterprise tier want <150ms p95 — fallback exceeds that. so multi-AZ reserved might be required for enterprise regions.
Maria: exactly. commercial tiers push us to accept the +8% cost in some regions (EU / APAC) to guarantee latency SLAs without model-quality regressions.
Jon: what about hybrid: keep reserved primary in 1 AZ and small emergency reserved in second AZ (say 10% of capacity) plus cross-AZ LB only for emergencies. that lowers fragmentation and limits egress.
Maria: i ran that — hybrid (10% cold-stack reserved) shows normalized cost = 1.03 and p99 for enterprise scenario ~120ms (within SLO). looks promising.
Ella: ok also consider cloud committed-use discounts (1yr vs 3yr) — 3yr nails price but reduces agility for model-version switching. ops/procurement needs to weigh that.
Priya: billing flag: note that egress shows up in network line items; we should map traffic flows to invoice SKUs next run to validate assumptions. last month the eu region had a mysterious "Inter-region transfer" line.
Maria: action items:
Maria: - i'll run a per-AZ invoice reconciliation for last 90d to map real inter-AZ GB (due Fri).
Maria: - @Priya please run a 10% hybrid reserved sim across EU-AZs with our current traffic (due Tue).
Maria: - @Max coordinate with solutions to figure cutoff for enterprise vs standard region placement (due next Thu).
Jon: +1. also add a quick column for disk-backed KV cold-start penalty (we saw 30-80ms extra per request).
Priya: noted.
Ella: sounds good. bump to planning doc once we have invoices. :thumbsup:
